before: "The Lord created me" (Proverbs 8:22). If you take "he created me" as referring to the divinity, it means "he appointed me." So too: "Create a clean heart in me, O God" (Psalm 50:12 LXX; Psalm 51:12 in modern Hebrew numbering). And: "that he might create the two in himself" (Ephesians 2:15). For it is not in essence that he might create those who had already come into being, but that he might appoint them. Therefore he appointed me as the beginning of his providential and creative works. And to David he says: "I was appointed king by him."
